subject.title: fix(security): bound hashFileContentsSync in approval script operand reads

question: Should OpenClaw preserve approval support for script operands larger than 8 MiB through a bounded-memory fingerprint path, or intentionally deny those operands?
rationale: The patch makes a new hard behavioral limit on an existing approval workflow, and no maintainer decision or documented contract in the supplied material establishes that this compatibility change is intended.

options.title: Preserve large-script approval support
options.body: Replace the fixed rejection with a bounded-memory fingerprint design that retains approval and revalidation behavior for regular script operands of any supported size.

options.title: Adopt the 8 MiB policy
options.body: Confirm that scripts over 8 MiB are unsupported for approval, document the denial and recovery path, and add real-flow proof of the intended behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve large-script approval support
recommendation.body: Replace the fixed rejection with a bounded-memory fingerprint design that retains approval and revalidation behavior for regular script operands of any supported size.
